title: 3 REITs To Buy And Hold
description: You don’t have to understand it to do well over time. You just have to know what quality companies to buy and at what prices. See these 3 REITs to buy and hold.

title: Boston Properties (BXP) Q1 FFO and Revenues Surpass Estimates
description: Boston Properties (BXP) delivered FFO and revenue surprises of 0.65% and 4.13%, respectively, for the quarter ended March 2021. Do the numbers hold clues to what lies ahead for the stock?

title: Boston Properties (BXP) Q1 FFO and Revenues Beat Estimates
description: Boston Properties' (BXP) Q1 performance displays better-than-anticipated portfolio performance and higher fee income.

title: Boston Properties Inc (BXP) Q1 2021 Earnings Call Transcript
description: BXP earnings call for the period ending March 31, 2021.

title: American Tower (AMT) Q1 AFFO Beats Estimates, Revenues Lag
description: Strong organic tenant billing growth in Q1 supports American Tower's (AMT) Q1 results. However, a decline in revenues in the Asia Pacific property segment acts as a spoilsport.

title: Extra Space Storage (EXR) Q1 FFO Tops Estimates, Revenues Miss
description: Robust average occupancy aids same-store net operating income growth for Extra Space Storage (EXR) in Q1.

title: Equinix (EQIX) Q1 FFO Surpasses Estimates, Revenues Meet
description: Equinix (EQIX) registers strong revenue growth across the Americas, EMEA and the Asia Pacific. It becomes the market leader in retail colocation in all these three regions.

title: Welltower (WELL) Q1 FFO Beats Estimates, Occupancy Up in April
description: While a fall in rental income, and revenues from resident fees and services impede Welltower's (WELL) Q1 top-line growth, it sees occupancy gains in April at its SHO portfolio.

title: Vornado (VNO) Q1 FFO Tops Estimates, Revenues & NOI Down Y/Y
description: Occupancy erosions in first-quarter 2021 hinder Vornado's (VNO) same-store NOI growth for the New York portfolio as well as theMART.

title: OUTFRONT Media (OUT) Q1 Adjusted FFO Deficit Comes as Expected
description: While Outfront Media (OUT) registers a fall in operating expenses in Q1, lower average revenues per display and the pandemic's impact on customer advertising expenditure act as deterrents.

title: Host Hotels (HST) Q1 FFO Beats Estimates, RevPAR Down Y/Y
description: While leisure demand for Host Hotels' (HST) luxury resorts in the Sunbelt and other key destinations aid the top line, hotel RevPAR and room revenue declines across all three businesses mar results.

title: Healthpeak (PEAK) Q1 FFO Surpasses Estimates, Revenues Miss
description: Healthpeak (PEAK) Q1 results reflect revenue growth. However, weakness in the CCRC portfolio affects results.

title: Iron Mountain (IRM) Beats Q1 FFO Estimates, Hikes '21 View
description: While core storage business remains resilient in Q1, Iron Mountain's (IRM) performance is affected by service revenue declines. The company hikes guidance for 2021.

title: Rayonier (RYN) Q1 Earnings Meet Estimates, Revenues Down Y/Y
description: Rayonier (RYN) registers growth in pro-forma operating income for all segments. Yet, the company witnesses a decline in revenues for first-quarter 2021.

title: Ventas (VTR) Q1 FFO Beats, Senior Housing Occupancy Dips
description: While Ventas' (VTR) office portfolio displays marginal net operating income growth, declining occupancy at its senior housing operating portfolio continues to be a deterrent in Q1.

title: Mack-Cali (CLI) Q1 FFO Tops Estimates, Revenues & NOI Dip Y/Y
description: While Mack-Cali's (CLI) multi-family residential portfolio sees decent leasing activity in the first quarter, the pandemic-led woes and high vacancy continue to dampen office portfolio performance.

Bloomberg reported Wednesday that deal volumes in Germany’s commercial real estate market dropped by 50%, to €14.9 billion ($16.2 billion), in the first half of 2023, the lowest levels seen since 2017. 
Similar tendencies have been noticed in other European countries, including Sweden, Ireland, and the United Kingdom, where buyers and sellers are unable to reach an agreement on pricing.
The impact of rising interest rates, which have increased borrowing costs and increased demand for yields among potential property investors, is considered the fundamental cause of this drop.
Despite falling bid prices, property owners are still unwilling to accept significant discounts to book values due to concerns about prospective debt ratio increases.
This has led to a frozen commercial real estate market where a big gap separates buyers and sellers. The longer it goes on, the more likely it is that it will end in favor of the buyers.

Even more concerning, the majority of participants surveyed by Bloomberg expect that U.S. commercial real estate prices won’t hit rock bottom until the latter half of 2024 or beyond, indicating a slow and persistent slump. 
This forecast spells trouble for the $1.5 trillion of commercial real estate debt due by the end of 2025, particularly for the 25% tied to office buildings. 
Already, a Green Street index shows a 16% drop in commercial property prices since their peak in March 2022.
